Definition: accusative case of G5485 as preposition; through favor of, i.e. on account of:--be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully.
BiblicalUsage: Charin is a small preposition, through favour of, on account of, for the sake of, and it carries the reason for things. Her sins are forgiven, for she loved much, and for this cause Paul bows his knees unto the Father. Cain slew his brother because his own works were evil and his brother's righteous.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the little word does heavy work: it tells me why forgiveness came, why Paul knelt, and why the first murder happened.
